title: Proof of tau M asymptotic rep theory
html:
Proof

Proof (Lean: tau_M_asymptotic_rep_theory). The factorisation defines F_\lambda; the substance lies in the parity and the proved rungs.

Parity (even in \hbar_q). Markov cyclicity \mathrm{tr}_M(xy) = \mathrm{tr}_M(yx) with the bar involution q \leftrightarrow q^{-1} forces F_\lambda(\hbar_q) = F_\lambda(-\hbar_q). The single-wrap character symmetrises over the two eigenphases of \rho_\lambda into \mathrm{tr}\,\rho_\lambda(\beta)\cdot\cos\alpha (prop:hoefsmit-V21-cos-symmetrization, prop:q-beta-cos-resummation). Since the cosine function is even, the rung exponents u_\lambda^k = b_\lambda^k\hbar_q^{2k} are even in \hbar_q by construction. The bar-parity alternation of the rung coefficients (\overline{c_k} = (-1)^k c_k, with bar-even seed c_2 = -1) is the sorry-free esymm_bar_parity of prop:q-beta-c-k-recursion-from-habiro-q-difference. \square

Baseline c_0 = 0. At q = 1, we have \hbar_q = 0, and \rho_\lambda(\sigma_i) maps to the symmetric-group permutation matrix. Therefore, \mathrm{tr}_M^{V_\lambda} = \mathrm{Tr}\,\rho_\lambda(\beta) and F_\lambda(0) = 1, which gives c_0 = 0. \square

One-dimensional irreducible representations. For the trivial representation V_{(n)} and the sign representation V_{(1^n)}, \rho_\lambda(\sigma_i) is a scalar. The off-diagonal coupling vanishes (b_\lambda = 0, hence u_\lambda = 0), and the Markov-symmetrised character equals the bare character. Thus, F_\lambda \equiv 1. We document the one-dimensional closed forms in prop:hecke-1d-irrep-closed-form-character. \square

N=1 envelope (coupling b), V_{(2,1)}. The first non-trivial irreducible representation is the two-dimensional V_{(2,1)} of H_3. Its single \tilde f_1 Kashiwara edge carries weight b_\lambda = b. This produces the eigenphase shift -b\,\hbar_q^2/2, given by the \tilde f_1 matrix element in the seminormal basis multiplied by \hbar_q^2/2. The shift resums into the \cos(\alpha - b\hbar_q^2/2) envelope. This provides the N=1 result of prop:hoefsmit-V21-cos-symmetrization. \square

Second rung (production wire), V_{(2,1)}: c_2 = -1. The first product rung is (1 + c_2 u^2) with u = b\hbar_q^2. We prove the seed c_2 = -1 categorically through the bar-even constraint. This provides the factor (1 - u^2) = (1 - b^2\hbar_q^4), matching the second-order correction consumed by the production neutron (\mathfrak{Q}_\beta = \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{(N=1)}\cdot(1 - b^2\hbar_q^4), derived_masses.q_beta_kashiwara_n2_mev). A single coupling b thus drives both the N=1 envelope and the proved second rung. \square

The proof determines c_0, the one-dimensional triviality, the N=1 coupling b, and the proved seed c_2 = -1, alongside the \hbar_q-parity. The rungs c_k^{(\lambda)} for k \geq 3 are generated by the proved recursion of prop:q-beta-c-k-recursion-from-habiro-q-difference once its kernel R(q,\xi) is fixed. That kernel remains open. \blacksquare
